rationale: This is the gen-4 conjunctive kink with the leverage leg swapped for share-count growth, and the "independent verification" claim is weakened by the fact that csho growth is mechanically driven by the same sstk/prstkc flows already in the signal, so the MIN weight partly restates the conditioning variable rather than validating it.

Averaging oancf/at with its own first difference inside an already-tested kink is a cosmetic weight tweak, and the orthogonality claim is wrong — DELTA(oancf/at,1) contains the current level with a positive loading, so this is close to a rescaled version of the existing level-weighted kink.

Redefining the flow as pure net shareholder payout (a real scope change, not a weight swap, and close to but not identical with published net-payout-yield work since it is asset-scaled and quality-kinked), though the reviewer should note that adding always-nonnegative dvt shifts the zero threshold so the indicator will largely partition dividend payers from non-payers rather than capital returners from raisers.

The weight RANK(NEG((ib-oancf)/at)) is mechanically dominated by oancf and therefore is largely a re-parameterization of the already-tested cash-profitability weight in the identical kink structure, so it cannot deliver the claimed independence from the profitability channel.

Earnings volatility is a genuinely distinct (second-moment) conditioning dimension not yet used inside the kink, and the diagnosis of why the gen-0 weakest-link version failed is credible, though this remains the Nth weight substitution in a heavily mined structural family and coverage will suffer from the 5-year window.

Replacing oancf with MA(oancf,3) in an already-tested ratio is precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and it does not address the more likely cause of the alpha/FMB gap — the exploding, sign-unstable behavior of the ratio when the denominator floor binds.
